strategy.summary: Reproduce the PR #17694 theta defect by building astropy from source at buggy commit 740147ed4504, applying the developer's test diff, and running test_to_physicsspherical_small_theta. On the buggy revision theta is computed via arccos(z/r), which for rho=1 m, z=1e8 m rounds to exactly 1.0 in float64, so theta collapses to 0 and the assert_allclose check against 1e-8 rad fails. On the fixed revision (arctan2(rho, z)) theta is about 1e-8 rad and the test passes. The environment is a source build, not the PyPI wheel, because the transition only exists in the repository revisions.
strategy.reproducing_test: astropy/coordinates/tests/test_representation.py::test_to_physicsspherical_small_theta (added method in the same test class as test_to_physicsspherical_at_the_origin, per the supplied diff)
strategy.success_criterion: On buggy commit 740147ed4504 with the test diff applied, the test FAILS because got.theta is about 0 rad (arccos of a value that rounds to 1.0) and assert_allclose against 1e-8 rad exceeds rtol 1e-7. On the fixed revision (arctan2(rho, z)) the same test PASSES. The transition fail-to-pass is the whole criterion.

risks: The README pip install astropy path installs a PyPI release, not the buggy commit; the reproduction requires a source build at 740147ed4504 and the buggy behaviour is only confirmed for that revision.

Python version and numpy version are not stated in the evidence; the arccos rounding mechanism is IEEE-deterministic, but a very new or old numpy could change SIMD arccos edge handling, so the test should be run on the build environment actually used.
The buggy theta value is not stated in the passages; the expected failure mode (theta = 0) is inferred from float64 arithmetic and should be verified by running the test on the buggy revision.
Exact magnitude at which the defect becomes visible is not stated beyond 'within milliarcseconds'; the only confirmed trigger is the rho=1 m, z=1e8 m case in the test.
The reproduction depends on a C compiler and the Cython/extension build; a build failure on the buggy commit would not show the numerical transition and must not be mistaken for it.
No platform-specific behaviour is evidenced, so the defect is expected to reproduce on any IEEE-754 platform; it is not known to require a particular architecture or sanitiser.
The test class containing test_to_physicsspherical_at_the_origin is not named in the evidence, so the test is selected with -k rather than by full node id.

oracle.reference_source: analytic theta = atan(rho/z) = 1e-8 rad, as written in the added test
oracle.why: Test compares computed theta to an analytic value; the buggy arccos path cannot resolve a value this small near the pole.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: Buggy code returns theta approximately 0 (arccos of z/r rounding to 1.0), so assert_allclose(got.theta, 1e-8 rad) raises AssertionError because the difference of 1e-8 rad exceeds rtol times 1e-8 rad.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: Fixed code computes theta = arctan2(1, 1e8) = 1e-8 rad to full float64 precision, within rtol 1e-7; r and phi assertions also pass.
